messages.author: 839dfa09184985a5
messages.subject: fvar/matrix
parts:
I've implemented a lot of fvar/matrix (and it's all tested and in master already)--only 29.7 Linear Algebra Functions and Solvers left.

I've run into a few things:

1) columns_dot_product, rows_dot_product, columns_dot_self, and rows_dot_self are all implemented in fvar/matrix (I did this one), agrad, and math/matrix, but not in the doc at all. Is it ok to doc these or are we waiting on something else? As a side note, columns and rows dot product are also in function signatures but not in any compiled model tests. If these are ready, I can go ahead and finish up the doccing/testing.

2) operator/ isn't doced either; this should be the division of a matrix/vector/row vector by a scalar. If these are ready too, I can doc them and add them to the appropriate tests.

3) Should I be implementing array operations too? (i.e. Ch28 of the manual)

4) Are there any other functions that need to be implemented for fvar/matrix that aren't in the doc?



Thanks,
Peter

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] fvar/matrix (& spec functions for CDFs?)
parts:
On 4/19/13 9:27 AM, Peter Li wrote:
> I've implemented a lot of fvar/matrix (and it's all tested and in master already)--only 29.7 Linear Algebra Functions and Solvers left.

That's fantastic. The solvers are actually
relatively easy because there are fewer signatures.

To make them efficient, you need to do the same kind
of explicit derivative calcs that are in the reverse-mode
code. Feel free to implement them simply with tests first,
then make them more efficient later. In fact, I'd strongly
recommend that as a development practice in general.

> I've run into a few things:
>
> 1) columns_dot_product, rows_dot_product, columns_dot_self, and rows_dot_self are all implemented in fvar/matrix (I did this one), agrad, and math/matrix, but not in the doc at all. Is it ok to doc these or are we waiting on something else? As a side note, columns and rows dot product are also in function signatures but not in any compiled model tests. If these are ready, I can go ahead and finish up the doccing/testing.

Yes, please go ahead and doc them if you have the time.
I was going to do it, but I'm swamped with admin for grants
and papers in prep. Marcus just added those functions, so
they're not part of the current release, but go into the next
one.
> 2) operator/ isn't doced either; this should be the division of a matrix/vector/row vector by a scalar. If these are ready too, I can doc them and add them to the appropriate tests.

Good catch for operator/ -- please doc that, too. We must've
missed it in the last round.
> 3) Should I be implementing array operations too? (i.e. Ch28 of the manual)
Yes, array operations, too.
> 4) Are there any other functions that need to be implemented for fvar/matrix that aren't in the doc?

I think you've done a better job than me of finding these!

The only functions/signatures that a Stan program can use are the
ones declared in gm/function_signatures.hpp
Of course, a C++ program can call anything that's public and includeable.

I believe there are more special functions that Michael
included for the CDFs that haven't been added to function signatures
and doc. Is that right, Michael? If so, are they isolated in
the code somewhere that'd make them easy to add.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] fvar/matrix (& spec functions for CDFs?)
parts:
No, the doc should be as is, because it's from
the perspective of the user of the Stan language.

The translator is from the modeling language to the
C++ functions inserts the elt_multiply or regular
matrix multiply or just plain old * where appropriate.

So elt_multiply and elt_divide also don't need to
go in function_signatures.

- Bob
